judgment.notes: N004's final bound applies to the fixed mean-zero f,w with their stated delta, M and timestep bounds. N005 applies on [t_n,t], whose endpoints are nonnegative and length is at most tau<=1; its static estimates are used at gamma and zero, with the zero-length case treated by its explicit zero integral clause. Its product estimate applies to (partial_x S_t A,S_t A) using the H^(1+gamma) and H^a stage bounds, and to (S_t w,S_t F_n). N006's normal-form identities are applied to smooth mean-zero pairs (f,f) and (f,F_n); its asymmetric J bound is used after symmetry with F_n in the inverse-derivative slot. All premises are available. No E or native M application occurs.

The endpoint formula has coefficient 1/6; bilinear subtraction gives the H^1 difference estimate, and 0<=a_gamma<=1 transfers it to H^a. Together with N005 this gives the small stage norms. The z_n X bound follows from z_n'=B_t(f,f)/2 and N006. The displayed exact-data product estimate and H^1 difference-of-squares estimate prove the strong B(F_n,F_n) bound; integration and N004 then bound Q_n,W_n. Differentiating the definitions gives the displayed Y_n' and zero initial value. Splitting f=w+(f-w) proves the Dinv B(f,F_n) bound, so integration gives both inverse-derivative defect bounds. Integration by parts with (f,F_n), F_n(t_n)=0 and F_n'=B(f,f)/2 gives exactly the exported C_n identity. Symmetry and the asymmetric J estimate bound its endpoint term by C_M q_n; trilinearity and N005 bound its integral term by C_M(tau^gamma+delta_n). Thus Y_n=C_n+Q_n-(t-t_n)W_n/tau is small in L2. All these objects are mean-zero; N006 converts their inverse-derivative bounds to H^(-pstar), which together with the strong L2 bound gives X. Every N008 clause follows, without an H^gamma bound on f.
